outcomes.text: Describe how light microscopes and stains show cells, and calculate magnification.
Explain how the parts of plant, animal and bacterial cells suit their jobs.
Explain how electron microscopes improved understanding of sub-cellular structures.

topics.title: B1.2 What happens in cells (and what do cells need)?

outcomes.text: Describe DNA as a polymer.
Describe DNA as two strands forming a double helix.
Describe DNA's four nucleotides, each with a sugar, phosphate and one base, and base pairing A-T and G-C.
Give a simple account of protein synthesis: transcription to mRNA, then translation with tRNA carrying amino acids.
Explain simply how the DNA triplet code decides the order of amino acids in a protein.
Describe experiments that investigate enzyme-catalysed reactions and how conditions change their rate.
Explain how enzymes work, including the active site, specificity and effects of temperature and pH.
Describe respiration as a universal process that supplies ATP in all living cells.
Describe respiration as an exothermic reaction.
Compare aerobic and anaerobic respiration in plants, fungi and animals.
Explain how sugars are used to build and break down carbohydrates.
Explain how amino acids are used to build and break down proteins.
Explain how fatty acids and glycerol are used to build and break down lipids.
Describe photosynthetic organisms as the main producers of food and biomass on Earth.
Describe photosynthesis, with its reactants and products.
Describe photosynthesis as an endothermic reaction.
Describe experiments that investigate photosynthesis.
Explain how temperature, light intensity and carbon dioxide concentration affect photosynthesis rate.
Explain how these factors interact as limiting factors on photosynthesis rate.
Explain how substances cross cell membranes by diffusion, osmosis and active transport.
Describe mitosis in growth, including the stages of the cell cycle.
Explain why cell differentiation matters.
Recall that stem cells exist in embryonic and adult animals and meristems in plants.
Describe what stem cells and meristems do in animals and plants.
Describe the difference between embryonic and adult stem cells in animals.
Explain why large organisms need exchange surfaces and transport systems, using surface area to volume ratio.
Describe substances that different organisms must move in and out for their needs.
Describe the human circulatory system and its link to gas exchange.
Explain how the heart and blood vessels are adapted to their functions.
Explain how red blood cells and plasma suit their transport roles.
Explain how plants take up water and mineral ions, linking root hair cell structure to function.
Describe transpiration and translocation.
Explain how xylem and phloem are adapted to their functions.
Explain how environmental factors affect the rate of water uptake by a plant.
Describe how a simple potometer investigates factors affecting water uptake.

topics.title: B3.1 Coordination and control - the nervous system

outcomes.text: Describe the structure of the nervous system.
Explain how nervous system parts produce a coordinated response.
Explain how a reflex arc's structure relates to its function.
Explain how the main structures of the eye relate to their functions.
Describe common eye defects and how some can be treated.
Describe the structure and function of the brain.
Explain why brain function is hard to investigate.
Explain limitations in treating brain damage and disease.

topics.title: B3.2 Coordination and control - the endocrine system

outcomes.text: Describe how the endocrine system coordinates and controls the body with hormones.
Explain the roles of thyroxine and adrenaline, with thyroxine as negative feedback.
Describe the role of hormones in human reproduction, including the menstrual cycle.
Explain how FSH, LH, oestrogen and progesterone interact in the menstrual cycle.
Explain hormonal contraception and evaluate hormonal and non-hormonal methods.
Explain how hormones are used in treating infertility.
Explain how plant hormones control and coordinate growth.
Describe the effects of plant hormones such as on shoots, roots, fruit and germination.
Describe ways people use plant hormones.
Explain why a constant internal environment must be kept despite changes.
Describe how the skin controls body temperature.
Explain how insulin controls blood sugar.
Explain how glucagon works with insulin to control blood sugar.
Compare type 1 and type 2 diabetes and how they are treated.
Explain the effect of osmotic changes in body fluids on cells.
Describe how the kidneys maintain water balance.
Describe the gross structure of the kidney and of a nephron.
Describe how ADH changes the permeability of the kidney tubules.
Explain the body's response to different temperature and osmotic challenges.
Recall that materials cycle between the abiotic and biotic parts of an ecosystem.
Explain the role of microorganisms in cycling materials.
Explain the importance of the carbon cycle and the water cycle to living things.
Explain how temperature, water content and oxygen affect decay rate.
Describe the levels of organisation in an ecosystem, from organism to ecosystem.
Explain how abiotic and biotic factors affect communities.
Describe interdependence and competition in a community.
Describe the differences between trophic levels.
Describe pyramids of biomass and explain, with examples, how biomass is transferred.
Calculate the efficiency of biomass transfer between trophic levels.

units.title: Topic B5: Genes, inheritance and selection

outcomes.text: Explain the terms gamete, chromosome, gene, allele, dominant, recessive, homozygous, heterozygous, genotype and phenotype.
Describe the genome as the entire genetic material of an organism.
Describe how the genome and environment together shape phenotype.
Recall that variants arise from mutations, most with no effect on phenotype.
Describe how genetic variants may influence phenotype.
Explain advantages and disadvantages of asexual and sexual reproduction.
Explain the terms haploid and diploid.
Explain how meiosis halves chromosome number to make gametes.
Explain single gene inheritance in homozygous and heterozygous crosses.
Predict the results of single gene crosses using Punnett squares.
Describe sex determination in humans with a genetic cross.
Recall that most features result from many genes, not one.
Describe how understanding of genetics has developed.
State that species populations usually contain extensive genetic variation.
Describe how biological developments have changed classification systems.
Explain how natural selection of variants best suited to the environment drives evolution.
Describe evolution as change in the inherited characteristics of a population, possibly forming new species.
Describe evidence for evolution such as fossils and antibiotic resistance in bacteria.
Describe the work of Darwin and Wallace on evolution by natural selection.

topics.title: B6.1 Monitoring and maintaining the environment

outcomes.text: Explain how to run a field investigation of distribution and abundance of organisms.
Describe positive and negative human impacts in ecosystems and their effect on biodiversity.
Explain benefits and challenges of maintaining local and global biodiversity.
Evaluate the evidence for the impact of environmental change.
Describe biological factors affecting food security.
Describe and explain agricultural solutions to food demand.
Describe biotechnological solutions to food demand.
Explain the impact of selectively breeding food plants and domesticated animals.
Describe genetic engineering as modifying an organism's genome to add desirable characteristics.
Describe the main steps of genetic engineering, including restriction enzymes, ligase and host bacteria.
Explain benefits and risks of gene technology in agriculture.
Describe the relationship between health and disease.
Describe different types of disease.
Describe how different diseases interact, such as HIV and tuberculosis.
Explain how pathogens cause communicable disease and spread in animals and plants.
Explain how spread of communicable disease can be reduced or prevented.
Describe a common human infection, a plant disease and sexually transmitted infections including HIV.
Describe physical plant defences against disease.
Describe chemical plant defences, such as antimicrobial substances.
Describe how plant diseases are detected and identified.
Explain how white blood cells and platelets suit their defence functions.
Describe the body's non-specific defences against pathogens.
Explain the immune system's role in defence.
Describe how monoclonal antibodies are produced.
Describe uses of monoclonal antibodies.
Explain the use of vaccines and medicines to prevent and treat disease.
Explain the aseptic techniques used when culturing organisms.
Describe how new medicines are discovered and developed, including preclinical and clinical testing.
Recall that many non-communicable diseases are caused by several interacting factors.
Evaluate treatments for cardiovascular disease.
Analyse how lifestyle factors affect incidence of non-communicable disease locally, nationally and globally.
Describe cancer as changes in cells that cause uncontrolled growth and division.
Discuss benefits and risks of stem cells in medicine.
Explain benefits and risks of gene technology in medicine.
Discuss why understanding the human genome matters for medicine.
